The latest evening news ratings show ABC is still ahead of its main rivals CBS and NBC - but the networks are starting to close the gap.

For the week of April 6, ABC maintained its lead in both total viewers and the key adults 25–54 demographic, while CBS and NBC lagged behind, according to new Nielsen data. “ABC World News Tonight,” anchored by David Muir, averaged 8.417 million total viewers and 1.067 million in that demographic for the week. That performance marked a slight dip from the previous week, with total viewership down 2 percent and the key demo unchanged. However, the broadcast showed strong year-over-year growth, rising 12 percent in total viewers and 5 percent in the key demo compared to the same week in 2025.

“NBC Nightly News,” anchored by Tom Llamas, averaged 6.434 million total viewers and 909,000 in the key adults 25–54 demographic for the week. The broadcast saw a noticeable week-over-week decline, dropping 4 percent in total viewers and 13 percent in the key demo. Despite that short-term dip, NBC posted year-over-year gains, increasing 6 percent in total viewers and 7 percent in the demo compared to the same week last year.

“CBS Evening News” with Tony Dokoupil continued to lag behind its rivals during the week of April 6, averaging 3.807 million total viewers and 477,000 in the adults 25–54 demographic. The numbers took a noticeable dip from the week before, with viewership down 8 percent overall and falling an even steeper 16 percent among younger viewers. Compared to the same time last year, total viewers ticked up slightly by 2 percent, but the key demo dropped 3 percent, underscoring the network’s ongoing struggle to win over a younger audience.

Meanwhile, “ABC World News Tonight” delivered a standout performance on April 10 with special live coverage of the Artemis II return to Earth. Anchored by Muir, the broadcast drew 9.77 million total viewers and 2.362 million in the key demo, making it the most-watched program of the night.

‘ABC World News Tonight,’ anchored by David Muir (left), was the most-watched evening newscast for the week of April 6, followed by ‘NBC Nightly News,’ anchored by Tom Llamas (middle) and ‘CBS Evening News,’ with Tony Dokoupil (right) ( Social media )

Other networks trailed significantly during that special coverage window. Fox News drew 4.999 million total viewers and 543,000 in the demo, while CBS News followed with 4.585 million viewers and 843,000 in the demo, according to the data.

NBC News aired its own coverage, bringing in 3.912 million total viewers and 946,000 in the key demographic.

CBS, in particular, has been under scrutiny following its recent overhaul of the “Evening News” anchored by Dokoupil and shaped by editor-in-chief Bari Weiss. Insiders say tensions are growing at CBS News as Weiss and CBS President Tom Cibrowski clash over how to improve ratings. The two have sharply different visions, with one staffer describing their dynamic to the New York Post last week as “the odd couple.” Cibrowski is reportedly pushing a “softer” editorial approach aimed at a Middle America appeal, while Weiss is advocating for a more aggressive, digital-first strategy focused on hard news and enterprise reporting.

NBC, meanwhile, has stayed comfortably in second place, with “Nightly News” showing steady performance since Llamas took over from Lester Holt in June. That said, the network is still working to broaden its appeal, especially among younger viewers, as it competes with “ABC World News Tonight,” anchored by Muir. NBC is leaning heavily on Llamas’ background as a former ABC correspondent and someone once seen as a potential successor to Muir to refresh its image.

Part of that push includes extending his presence beyond the traditional broadcast. Llamas also hosts the streaming companion program “Top Story” right after “Nightly News,” a move designed to keep viewers engaged longer and reach audiences who are increasingly getting their news beyond traditional TV.

News.title: O’Sullivan plots path to Higgins after pushing World Snooker Championship debutant to the brink
News.content:
Ronnie O’Sullivan has taken a giant step towards a mouth-watering second round match against fellow 50-year-old John Higgins with a highly impressive start to his quest for an eighth world snooker title.

Despite initially heading for the wrong table on his return to the Crucible, O’Sullivan looked instantly back at home following a mixed season spent largely outside of England that has contained recent hints of a return to form.

O’Sullivan raced to a 5-0 lead before sharing the final four frames of the opening session of his first round match against China’s He Guoqiang to lead 7-2 ahead of the conclusion on Wednesday afternoon.

Although O’Sullivan did reach the semi-final last year, he looked bereft of confidence with what was a new cue before being comprehensively outplayed by the eventual winner Zhao Xintong.

Despite another year and a few more grey hairs, it was instantly obvious that O’Sullivan arrives in Sheffield this year rather happier with both his form and chances of moving clear of Stephen Hendry to become the only eight-times world champion in the modern era.

It helped that Guoqiang missed a series of early chances in what was a wide-open match, but O’Sullivan’s usual break-building fluency was crucially also matched by some well struck long pots and clearances when the balls were not always invitingly placed.

The early burst of frames included breaks of 72, 97 and 113 before Guoqiang’s brief fightback was halted by further runs of 52 and 86.

Should O’Sullivan complete the expected victory, the second round will be a rerun of the final against Higgins exactly 25 years ago, which he won 18-14 to win his first world title.

Higgins and Mark Williams, the third 50-plus member of the Class ‘92, are respectively going for their fifth and fourth world title.

Although O’Sullivan has now slipped furthest down the rankings, that is largely explained by his much more limited tournament schedule. There have been encouraging signs in recent months, however, with O’Sullivan following up his 153 total clearance in the International Open in China with a resounding victory against Higgins in the final of the invitational John Virgo Trophy in Ireland last week.

News.title: Wage growth slumps to five-year low
News.content:
Workers are seeing the slowest pay rises in more than five years in a blow to households already facing soaring bills triggered by the war in Iran.

Average wages grew by 3.6pc in the three months to February, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS). This was the weakest rise since the quarter to November 2020.

Adjusting for inflation, British workers’ pay increased by only 0.2pc.

Slowing wages will raise the pressure on families, as the war in Iran pushes up the cost of living.

The ongoing conflict is expected to drive up food inflation to more than 9pc by the end of the year, according to forecasts by the Food and Drink Federation. Average households energy bills are expected to rise close to £2,000 a year, while petrol and diesel prices have already spiked.

Martin Beck, chief economist at WPI Strategy, said: “Weaker pay growth will compound the squeeze on households from higher energy prices and supply chain disruption linked to the conflict in the Middle East.

“While recent diplomatic developments may limit the worst-case outcomes, a period of falling real wages is still likely in the second half of the year, weighing on consumer spending and, in turn, labour demand.”

The public sector is better protected, with wages still growing by 5.2pc annually compared with a rise of 3.2pc in the private sector.

Unemployment surprisingly fell before the conflict, the ONS said, though it remains the hardest time since Covid to find a job with far more jobseekers than open roles.

The jobless rate fell to 4.9pc in December to February, down from 5.1pc in the previous three months.

Economists said the fall was mainly driven by rising economic inactivity, meaning they are no longer classified as unemployed, rather than more people finding work.

Modupe Adegbembo at Jefferies said: “This apparent improvement was entirely flattered by falling participation rather than stronger hiring. The decline in labour force participation mechanically reduced the unemployment rate, masking continued softness in actual labour demand.”

The number of employees on the nation’s payroll fell by 65,000 in the year to March.

Job losses have been concentrated among younger workers, with 242,000 fewer people under the age of 35 in work since since Rachel Reeves’s maiden Budget in October 2024, ONS figures show. By contrast, there are almost 100,000 more people aged 35 and older employed compared to October 2024.

There are now 2.5 unemployed people per vacancy, which makes it is the toughest time to find work since early 2021.

The number of advertised jobs fell to 711,000 in March, the lowest number in five years. Outside of the pandemic, vacancies are at an 11-year low.

News.title: One-in-three Russians should be tested for HIV every year, urges health minister
News.content:
A third of Russia’s population should be tested for HIV every year, its health minister has urged, in a sign an epidemic downplayed by the Kremlin is spiralling.

Mikhail Murashko said screening was essential to curb the transmission of the virus, which has exploded among Russian troops and the broader population since Moscow launched its invasion of Ukraine.

“Further expansion of medical testing is necessary. Every third citizen should be tested, with particular attention to at-risk groups,” the Russian Health Ministry quoted him as saying last week.

Since 2022, Russia has been in the top five countries for new HIV cases, according to the UN. Only South Africa, Mozambique, Nigeria and India had more.

When the figures were released, the Russian health ministry dismissed them as “provocative propaganda” and accused the UN of attempting to “falsify statistical data”.

While Russia has long had high rates of HIV, it now has the highest prevalence in Europe, with 890 cases per 100,000 people, according to World Health Organization (WHO) data. The rate is comparable to that of Liberia, Sierra Leone or Guinea.

An estimated 1.1 million Russians, or nearly one per cent of the population, are now living with the virus.

Experts warn the true figure may be much higher, given how many cases go undetected and unreported.

“Infection risks are very high,” said Vadim Pokrovsky, the head of Russia’s Federal Scientific and Methodological Centre for Aids Prevention and Control. “If we look only at adults aged 15 to 50, more than one per cent are infected – that is, every hundredth person.”

Among men in their early forties, the rate climbs to around one in 25, he added.

News.title: Severe malaria may do long-lasting damage to children’s brains, major study finds
News.content:
Severe malaria may be doing long-lasting damage to children’s brains, according to a major study in Uganda.

Researchers collected data on a group of nearly 1,000 children up to 15 years after infection and found that those who had survived cerebral malaria or severe anaemia caused by malaria performed worse on cognitive tests many years later.

Cerebral malaria is considered the most severe form of the disease and occurs when infected blood cells get stuck inside small blood vessels in the brain, restricting blood flow and causing swelling, often leading to a coma and death.

Along with anaemia, it is believed to affect up to two million children each year, mostly in sub-Saharan Africa, causing hundreds of thousands of deaths.

The research, which was published in the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) last week, is the latest in a series of studies on the impact of severe malaria led by Paul Bangira of the Makerere University Hospital in Kampala, Uganda, and Chandy John of Indiana University.

Known as the Malarial Impact on Neurobehavioral Development (MIND) study, the researchers have been following the same cohort of 1,438 children since 2008.

The first study found that children who had cerebral malaria scored lower on cognitive tests two years after their infection while a second, carried out between 2014 and 2018, confirmed these results.

The most recent test began in 2020, with the researchers hoping to find out whether the children’s cognitive deficits had improved. They managed to track down 939 of the original cohort and had them sit tests in mathematics, reading, attention and overall cognition.

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham buys stake in £82million team in completely different sport as he becomes first individual to invest
Sports.content:
JUDE BELLINGHAM has bought a stake in a team worth £82million – and they play a completely different sport.

The Real Madrid and England superstar, 22, was born in Stourbridge, West Midlands.





And he put an estimated £800,000 of his reported £40m net worth back into a club near his hometown.

As revealed by The Times, Bellingham stumped up the cash to purchase a one per cent share of the Birmingham Phoenix Hundred cricket franchise.

Half of that was from Warwickshire County Cricket Club’s 51 per cent stake and the other half from Knighthead Capital Management LLC’s 49 per cent.

The £800,000 figure comes after Knighthead paid £40m for their 49 per cent share last year – making a total valuation of £82m.



Knighthead are also the owners of Birmingham City, Bellingham’s boyhood club.

The midfielder came through the youth ranks at St Andrew’s and made his first-team debut aged just 16.

The Blues retired his No22 upon his departure to Borussia Dortmund in 2020.

However, it could all have been very different.

Bellingham joined Birmingham aged eight but also played cricket as a youngster, starring for Hagley CC.

And by pumping money into Phoenix, he has proven his passion for both the West Midlands and cricket.

Bellingham went to Priory School, just a mile away from Edgbaston, home of Phoenix and Warwickshire.

His investment is the first from an individual into the Hundred.

It comes a year after Warwickshire told the ECB they were hoping to bring in another high-profile investor.



The Phoenix men’s team features England’s young stars Jacob Bethell and Rehan Ahmed.

They were runners-up in 2021 and finished third in 2024, while the women’s team’s best finish was third in 2021.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s son, 15, could play alongside dad as Al-Nassr ‘consider promoting star to first team’
Sports.content:
CRISTIANO RONALDO could yet make more history by playing alongside his son, Cristiano Ronaldo Jr, next season.

The 41-year-old is driving towards scoring 1,000 career goals needing just 31 more strikes to reach the immortal tally.





He is also set to play in the World Cup for Portugal this summer, which would be a record-breaking sixth appearance at the finals and he could also become the first player to score in six different World Cup finals.

Now, according to the Arab newspaper Al Wiam, his club Al Nassr is considering integrating his son into the first team squad next season.

Ronaldo Jr is still only 15-years-old, but he has played for Portugal‘s youth teams and won the U17 World Cup with them.

How good is he really? Ronaldo Jr has learned football at some of the best youth academies in the world following in his father’s career.

After training at Real Madrid, Juventus, and Manchester United youth teams, he now plays for Al Nassr.

On top of his international progress, Ronaldo Jr has consistently demonstrated his father’s keen eye for goal.

He netted 58 goals in 23 matches with Juventus’ U-9 team and 56 goals in 27 matches with Al Nassr’s U-15 team.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

After starring in the club’s youth set-up, Al Nassr will assess his development at the end of the season and if he is ready for first team action.



Should they decide he makes the grade, Ronaldo would repeat the feat of LeBron James in the NBA after he suited up for the LA Lakers alongside his son Bronny James Jr.

It has been done in football before, but only on a few occasions at the top level.

Notably, Eidur Gudjohnson replaced his father, Arnor, as a 17-year-old to make his debut for Iceland and both Rivaldo and Henrik Larsson played professional games with their sons in their respective homelands.

Ronaldo has one-year left on his contract and the Gulf State club have proven themselves wary of getting on the wrong side of their superstar name.

The striker went on strike earlier this season after objecting to the club’s transfer business as he watched former team-mate Karim Benzema join another rival.



However, the club are now eight points clear at the top of the league and on course to give Ronaldo a first league title since moving to the country back in 2023.

Sports.title: Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany turns down major World Cup job months before tournament starts
Sports.content:
BAYERN MUNICH manager Vincent Kompany has rejected the chance to be a pundit at this summer’s World Cup.

The Belgian, who has worked with broadcasters multiple times in the past dismissed the idea.





Highly regarded Italian reporter Fabrizio Romano posted on X today confirming the news.

He reported that in response to punditry offers Kompany said: “Absolutely no chance!”

“Why would I do that in vacation time? Then I wouldn’t have any family in Munich next season. No chance.”

So it seems that the Bayern manager intends to relax and re-energise with his family instead of offer his opinions in the USA.



He’s previously served as a pundit for the BBC, Sky Sports and TNT Sports – he was on the BBC’s panel at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar but missed the start because of a “visa blunder“.

But he does not fancy it off the back of a demanding season in charge of German giants Bayern Munich.

His side confirmed the Bundesliga title at the weekend following a 4-2 win over Stuttgart.

The Bavarians sit 15 points clear of second-placed Borussia Dortmund with four games remaining.



It’s Kompany’s second title in a row since joining Bayern in 2024.

They also have two semi-finals to overcome if they want to win the treble for the first time since 2020.

Bayern face Bayer Leverkusen in the DFB Pokal semi tomorrow before visiting Paris Saint Germain in the Champions League semi-final first leg next Tuesday 28 April.

Kompany’s team beat Real Madrid 6-4 on aggregate in the quarter-finals as late goals from former Premier League stars Luis Diaz and Michael Olise won them the tie in the second leg.

England star Harry Kane also scored in both legs – the Englishman has scored a staggering 51 goals in all competitions for Bayern this season and is current favourite with the bookies to win the Ballon d’Or.



His performance at the World Cup will no doubt influence his chances of winning the illustrious Fifa award.

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham buys stake in cricket team as Real Madrid star joins The Hundred
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham buys stake in cricket team as Real Madrid star joins The Hundred

Real Madrid and England star Jude Bellingham has invested in The Hundred side Birmingham Phoenix and is set to be unveiled on Wednesday as an owner

View 2 Images Jude Bellingham has made a move into cricket (Image: Alex Grimm, Getty Images)

Former Birmingham City star Jude Bellingham has acquired a 1% stake in the Birmingham Phoenix cricket team. The Real Madrid and England sensation is set to be confirmed as a co-owner of the Hundred franchise on Wednesday.

‌



The 22-year-old is reported to have secured a share worth at least £800,000 in the team that plays its home fixtures at Edgbaston. Bellingham is a well-known cricket enthusiast, having played at junior level for Hagley Cricket Club in Worcestershire.

‌



Birmingham Phoenix share a common owner with Birmingham City in the form of American investment group Knighthead Capital Management. American NFL legend Tom Brady also has ties with the group.

‌



The investment firm jointly owns Phoenix alongside Warwickshire. Knighthead acquired their stake in the Hundred outfit when the eight franchises were put up for sale last year, securing a 49% share for £48million, with Warwickshire holding on to a 51% stake.

According to the Times, Bellingham has purchased 0.5% from both Warwickshire and Knighthead respectively. The franchise is understood to be valued at around £82m.

‌



During the sale of The Hundred teams, Warwickshire made clear to the ECB that they planned to attract another high-profile investor. New owners would ordinarily be prohibited from offloading any shares for a period of five years. Should Bellingham have paid £800,000 for his 1% share, £80,000 of that would be redistributed via the ECB to grassroots cricket, with the bulk of the money split between Warwickshire and Knighthead Capital.

Last July, the ECB confirmed it had raised in excess of £500m, with £50m directed towards grassroots sport following the sale of stakes in six teams.

Another prominent football figure, Chelsea co-owner Todd Boehly, invested in the Trent Rockets through Cain International. He holds joint ownership of the company alongside fellow Chelsea director and co-owner Jonathan Goldstein, with the pair paying just under £40m for their 49% stake in the Nottingham-based side.

‌



View 2 Images Jude Bellingham is set to be announced as an owner of Birmingham Phoenix (Image: Grzegorz Wajda/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

The Sun Group, owners of Indian Premier League outfit Sunrisers Hyderabad, splashed more than £100m on a 100% stake in Northern Superchargers, based at Yorkshire's Headingley. Indian firm RPSG Group, who own Lucknow Super Giants in the IPL and Durban's Super Giants in the SA20, snapped up 70% of Manchester Originals, while Delhi Capitals owners GMR Group acquired 49% of Southern Brave.

US-based outfits Tech Titans and Washington Freedom completed their respective purchases of London Spirit and Welsh Fire. Speaking at the time, ECB chairman Richard Thompson said it was a seminal moment.

‌



"The Hundred has already played a vital role in growing cricket in England and Wales - attracting new audiences, elevating the women's game, and delivering high-quality entertainment," he said. "The sheer scale of global interest we've seen throughout this process highlights just how much potential remains to be unlocked.

"With these new partners on board, we're entering an exciting new phase and a seminal moment for cricket in England and Wales. Their global perspective and track record in elite sport and business will help us reimagine what's possible - from deepening fan connections to attracting even more world-class players.

"Crucially, this investment will not only fuel the competition's growth but also channel transformative levels of funding into our professional counties and grassroots game."

Sports.title: Paul Merson tips Cole Palmer to complete Man Utd transfer after Chelsea 'kick in the teeth'
Sports.content:
Paul Merson tips Cole Palmer to complete Man Utd transfer after Chelsea 'kick in the teeth'

Cole Palmer was the subject of intense transfer speculation during the January window, with Manchester United said to be keen on the Chelsea midfielder ahead of a potential summer move

View 2 Images Cole Palmer has been linked with a move to Manchester United (Image: Charlotte Wilson/Offside, Offside via Getty Images)

Paul Merson believes that Cole Palmer will make the switch to Manchester United if Chelsea fail to clinch Champions League qualification for 2026/27. The Wythenshawe-born star was the subject of intense speculation during the January transfer window, with United linked with a surprise swoop for him.

‌



Reports indicated that the Manchester City academy product was unhappy in the capital, and that he could head back to the north west once again to wear United red. However, such claims were dismissed by Liam Rosenior, who insisted that Palmer is settled at Stamford Bridge.

‌



The head coach, who assumed control from Enzo Maresca earlier this year, also maintained that the 23-year-old - who is tied to Chelsea until 2033 - is off limits. That's given his extensive contract and the price that the Blues would demand to allow him to depart.

‌



Cole Palmer caught exploding at Alejandro Garnacho after moment in Man Utd match READ MORE :

Cole Palmer ultimatum backfires and leaves Chelsea future in doubt after Man Utd links READ MORE :

However, as the campaign nears its conclusion, Merson claims that United could prove an appealing destination this summer should Chelsea miss out on Champions League football. Speaking with Sky Sports, the pundit said: "If Chelsea don't beat Brighton on Tuesday, they could be 11th by the end of the week.

"And do I expect them to beat Brighton on Tuesday? No. The only consolation is if they beat Brighton, then Nottingham Forest - then they have Liverpool in a must-win game.

"At that point you never know. But Chelsea don't play any other team in the top five apart from that. So you don't have the chance to gain any other points, and that's good news if you're a team in the top five, with five games to go.

‌



"No Champions League football will be a kick in the teeth for Chelsea. Do you think Cole Palmer will be at Chelsea playing in the Europa Conference League? I don't think so. Manchester United will get into the Champions League, and I wouldn't be surprised if he was playing there next season."

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Chelsea currently find themselves sitting sixth in the Premier League as they prepare for their final five fixtures of the campaign, level on points (48) with both Brentford and Bournemouth, though ahead on goal difference.

‌



With Liverpool sitting seven points above the Blues in fifth, clawing their way into the top five before the season wraps up looks like an incredibly tall order - and there remains a very real danger that Chelsea could yet slip further down the table before the curtain comes down with their final match against Sunderland AFC.

Manchester United, meanwhile, have enjoyed a remarkable revival under Michael Carrick during the second-half of the season - moving 10 points clear of Chelsea in third place after their win at Stamford Bridge with Champions League football for 2026/27 virtually secured.

View 2 Images Paul Merson thinks Cole Palmer could end up at Old Trafford (Image: Sky Sports)

Article continues below

With reinforcements for their midfield engine room high on the agenda this summer following Casemiro's impending departure, the Red Devils have been linked with a host of top-class talent in recent weeks.

However, if Merson's view is anything to go by, Palmer could emerge as the number one target over the coming months - though a tactical reshuffle would be required given Bruno Fernandes has, as ever, flourished in his favoured role behind the striker this campaign.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola has perfect three-word response to Declan Rice after title warning
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola has perfect three-word response to Declan Rice after title warning

Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice was quick to tell his team-mates that the Premier League title race isn't done despite losing to Manchester City - and it's now been seen by Pep Guardiola

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola was a fan of Declan Rice's actions after Manchester City's win over Arsenal (Image: Sky Sports)

Pep Guardiola says he 'loves' the message Declan Rice was seen relaying to his Arsenal team-mates on the pitch immediately after their damaging defeat against title rivals Manchester City.

‌



The England midfielder could be seen telling team-mates the title race is "not done" despite failing to make the most of an opportunity to kill off City with a win. Instead, Guardiola's side are three points behind Arsenal and could even usurp them on Wednesday night if they win their game in hand against Burnley, who are mired in the relegation zone.

‌



Asked about Rice's comments, Guardiola waxed lyrical about the mentality of the midfielder and his team-mates as they and Manchester City gear up for an all-out sprint to the finish.

‌



"I love that. I love that. That's why Arsenal is there," the City boss told Sky Sports.

Arsene Wenger issues new Premier League title prediction after Arsenal stumble READ MORE :

"I saw it [on Monday] and it shows what Declan Rice means. That's the Arsenal mentality, we've faced it in the Premier League these [past] seasons and in the Carabao Cup, how competitive they are.

"Otherwise they can't have done the season they have done in the Premier League being there and being unbeaten in the Champions League, as you have Mikel [Arteta] but also these type of players that follow the message.

‌



"And in the bad moments, they have the resilience [to say] we are there, we are there. That is a good example for us what we're going to face in the six games, five games [for them] in the title race."

View 2 Images Rice was seen telling team-mates "it's not done" in the aftermath of Arsenal's defeat (Image: Sky Sports)

Arsenal and Manchester City will be level on points if the latter defeat Burnley on Wednesday night, meaning it is still all to play for. The Gunners are seeking a first league title since 2004, while City are out to clinch a fifth domestic crown in six years.

‌



When he was then asked if he has shown his players the video clip of Rice saying 'it's not done', Guardiola replied: "They know exactly what opponents we're going to face in the five games for them, six for us.

"If people think because we beat them, the title race is done, Declan Rice showed us that they are there."

Sports.title: Eddie Howe faces crunch talks with PIF at Newcastle United meeting
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe faces crunch talks with PIF at Newcastle United meeting

Newcastle United head coach Eddie Howe has come under scrutiny following a difficult season in the Premier League for the Magpies and he is set to meet club chiefs next week

View 2 Images Eddie Howe's future has come under scrutiny (Image: Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe will have face-to-face talks with Magpies chiefs next week. Howe is under pressure following a difficult Premier League season but the Toon head coach will be contributing to a board meeting that has long been on the books.

‌



The 48-year-old will participate in a meeting with PIF officials, who are set to jet in from Riyadh, and give his view on performances and future planning as the season nears its end. Chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan will be present for the meeting, as will CEO David Hopkinson, financial chief Simon Capper and stadium boss Brad Miller, according to our sister title Chronicle Live.

‌



Rather than facilitating a vote of confidence in Howe's abilities, the club's new training ground and stadium projects are on the agenda. Several meetings of this type take place throughout the season, with Al-Rumayyan remaining hugely influential at St James' Park.

‌



The 56-year-old PIF governor has attended just a few games this season as the ownership look to empower Hopkinson and the rest of the board to deal with the day-to-day running of the club. For now, their plan appears to be ensuring that Howe and his coaches have everything they need to succeed.

After qualifying for the Champions League last season, Newcastle currently sit in 14th place. They are six points away from qualifying for European football and 11 clear of the relegation zone.

It is understood that Howe retains the support of Newcastle bosses, though all parties acknowledge that football is a results-driven business. Relationships are said to remain strong, and the plan is to provide Howe with time to turn things around.

‌



Newcastle have five games remaining in the Premier League season after reaching the quarter-finals of the Champions League and the Carabao Cup semi-final this season. Games against Arsenal, Brighton, Nottingham Forest, West Ham and Fulham remain as the Magpies look to bounce back from the defeats in a row in the division.

Plans are already being formed for the summer with a pre-season training camp in Europe anticipated rather than a long-haul summer tour to the United States or the Far East. The club do not want to further drain their players after the World Cup in the United States, with fewer commercial opportunities available following the sport's biggest event.

View 2 Images Newcastle have had a difficult season in the Premier League (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



Howe has also admitted he could be open to adding a new coach to his team in the summer. "Yeah, I'm open to anything," Howe told reporters last week.

"I certainly haven't got a fixed mindset or a closed mindset in terms of growth or improvement. In my current backroom there's healthy debate, there's healthy conflict and I think you need that.

"We've got staff that have been hugely successful for me and for us over a long period of time. I think you've got be very careful, in my position, not to throw out good things on the back of an over reaction to a shorter term problem.

Article continues below

"I think those decisions are best made in summer, every summer I'll sit down and think how we can healthily change things. I think change can sometimes be really, really good. I'm very open to anything. Let's see what happens."

Sports.title: Why Cole Palmer is missing from Chelsea squad vs Brighton in huge blow to Liam Rosenior
Sports.content:
Why Cole Palmer is missing from Chelsea squad vs Brighton in huge blow to Liam Rosenior

Chelsea face Brighton and Hove Albion in a pivotal match this evening, but they will have to face the Seagulls without star midfielder Cole Palmer

View 3 Images Cole Palmer will not feature against Brighton and Hove Albion (Image: Alex Pantling, Getty Images)

Cole Palmer has been left out of Chelsea's trip to Brighton for this evening's Premier League fixture due to a minor hamstring problem.

‌



The Blues desperately require victory at the Amex Stadium to maintain their faint Champions League qualification ambitions. Liverpool extended their advantage over Chelsea to seven points following their triumph against Everton on Sunday afternoon, less than 24 hours after Manchester United defeated the Blues by a single goal at Stamford Bridge.

‌



A dismal weekend places additional pressure on Chelsea to claim all three points tonight. Nevertheless, Liam Rosenior must attempt this without Palmer, who hasn't made the journey to the south coast owing to a hamstring complaint. Palmer will undergo assessment before this weekend's FA Cup semi-final encounter with Leeds United.

‌



Speaking earlier this month, Palmer said he had "turned a corner" regarding his fitness. The 23-year-old, who has managed just 10 goals across all competitions for the west Londoners this term, has been battling a complicated groin injury throughout most of the season.

When questioned by football.london whether he believed Palmer had turned a corner, Rosenior said: "If Cole feels that, that is great. Cole, as I've said many times before, is a top player who's gone through a really difficult period in terms of injury, in terms of the amount of games he's had.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"What I'm seeing in Cole now is a brightness, a freshness, and hopefully he can maintain that between now and the end of the season."

Joao Pedro continues to be sidelined with a thigh problem after the ex-Brighton striker was ruled out of Saturday's loss to Man United. It appears to be a back three/back five formation, with Trevoh Chalobah returning to the starting XI alongside fellow centre-backs Wesley Fofana and Jorrel Hato. Romeo Lavia is recalled to the team. Pedro Neto appears set to operate just behind striker Liam Delap at the Amex.

View 3 Images Cole Palmer has struggled with his fitness all season-long (Image: James Gill - Danehouse)

‌



Rosenior was brutally honest about the Blues' hopes of finishing in the top five this season. However, he has made it clear he and his players have not given up hope.

He said: "We’ve made it very difficult for ourselves. We have to be honest and realistic with that, but what we can’t do is give up. We have to keep fighting.

View 3 Images Rosenior spoke honestly about Chelsea's hopes of qualifying for the Champions League (Image: Darren Walsh, Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

‌



"We have to make sure we go to Brighton with similar attributes to what I saw against Manchester United in terms of our energy, intensity and engagement to the game, which was good. But we didn’t keep a clean sheet, and we didn’t take advantage of the chances, so we need to be more clinical and ruthless in both boxes."

Chelsea XI vs Brighton: Sanchez; Gusto, Fofana, Chalobah, Hato, Cucurella; Caicedo, Lavia, Fernandez; Neto, Delap

Sports.content:
Rodri, Gvardiol, Dias - Man City injury news and return dates after Pep Guardiola update

Manchester City will be hoping to take top spot in the Premier League with a win at Turf Moor against relegation-threatened Burnley

View 2 Images (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images)

Manchester City have the opportunity to go top of the Premier League with a victory over Burnley and Pep Guardiola will be carefully considering his options to find success. The Catalan coach will have to assess the conditions of figures such as Rodri and Ruben Dias as they look to have a perfect end to the season.

‌



Sunday's triumph over Arsenal has brought them to within three points of the league leaders with an inferior goal difference of one. Guardiola's men head to Turf Moor to face relegation-battling Burnley on Wednesday, a venue that has proved fruitful in recent seasons.

‌



For City, Wednesday presents a chance to maintain their momentum following the vital victory over their Premier League title challengers on Sunday after Erling Haaland's match-winning strike. With the Gunners navigating a difficult spell, City can pile the pressure on their North London opponents.

‌



Guardiola will not have all his players available, and he is sure to manage the minutes of some amid a busy week of action. There is little room for error at this stage of the season.

Mirror Football takes a look at City's fitness concerns heading into the clash against the Clarets.

Rodri

Rodri hobbled off during the 2-1 victory over Arsenal at the weekend. The midfielder went down clutching his groin in the closing stages of the match before being substituted by Nico Gonzalez, who may reclaim his spot in the starting XI owing to his unavailability.

‌



Guardiola expects Wednesday to come too soon for the Spaniard. He said: "I think for tomorrow he will not be ready.

"We'll see in the next games, [in the FA Cup] semi-final against Southampton or in 12, 13 days against Everton."

Potential return date: Southampton - FA Cup semi-final (April 25) or Everton (May 4).

‌



View 2 Images Rodri is set to miss Manchester City's clash at Burnley. (Image: Getty Images)

Ruben Dias

Ruben Dias is anticipated to stay out of action for the journey to East Lancashire following an ankle problem sustained at the start of April. The Portuguese centre-back has been missing from the first team since being withdrawn at the interval during the Champions League loss to Real Madrid.

Guardiola confirmed during Tuesday's press briefing that the fixture against the relegation-threatened side will arrive too early for Dias. The Manchester Evening News state that he is unlikely to return before the end of the month.

‌



Guardiola said: "He is not yet ready."

Potential return date: Everton (May 4).

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

‌



Josko Gvardiol

Josko Gvardiol is another Manchester City player who faces a battle against the clock to feature once more before another Premier League campaign draws to a close. The Croatian was withdrawn with a fractured leg during the home clash with Chelsea on January 4.

He has since had an operation and the expectation would have been to see him return to training before the season ends, but the probability is that he will be fully recovered for pre-season.

Potential return date: Pre-season 2026

Sports.title: Liverpool injury latest: Ekitike, Mamardashvili and Alisson updates before Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
Liverpool injury latest: Ekitike, Mamardashvili and Alisson updates before Crystal Palace

Liverpool play host to Crystal Palace at Anfield on Saturday afternoon as they vie for a strong finish to the season to secure European football in 2026/27

View 4 Images Giorgi Mamardashvili was injured during the Merseyside Derby (Image: Jacques Feeney/Offside, Offside via Getty Images)

Liverpool welcome Crystal Palace to Anfield on Saturday afternoon, but could be missing a raft of key players. Arne Slot is feeling the strain of a congested fixture list, with several of his first-choice stars unavailable due to various injuries.

‌



At such a crucial juncture of the season, the Reds will need to be virtually flawless between now and next month to guarantee their spot in Europe for 2026/27. Liverpool currently sit fifth in the Premier League standings as they approach their final five fixtures against Palace, Manchester United, Chelsea, Aston Villa and Brentford.

‌



Compounding the pressure, each of their rivals following this weekend's encounter with Palace are also vying for Champions League qualification for next term. While Slot would have hoped to have a full complement of players at his disposal as Liverpool chase a frantic finale, the Dutchman faces a substantial injury list to contend with.

‌



Yan Diomande to Liverpool transfer threat emerges after talks held over £87m deal READ MORE :

Jamie Carragher shares what he has heard about Arne Slot's Liverpool future READ MORE :

Here, Mirror Football looks at all of the latest Liverpool injury updates ahead of Saturday's clash at Anfield...

Hugo Ekitike

Hugo Ekitike has undergone surgery on an Achilles tendon rupture he sustained during last week's Champions League reverse with Paris Saint-Germain on home soil. Not only is the Frenchman out for the rest of the season, but he will also miss this summer's Alisson.

Liverpool will also be without the forward for half of next season should reports suggesting he faces nine months on the sidelines prove accurate. Reflecting on Ekitike's misfortune, Slot said: "Devastating for him coming to a new club and having so much impact straight away.

‌



"Playing against your former club in the Champions League quarter-final with so much to come for him in the summer. First thoughts are with him being out for such along time, missing out on so many special moments.

View 4 Images Hugo Ekitike suffered a serious Achilles injury against PSG on Tuesday (Image: Getty Images)

"Not the first and not the last player who experienced something like this at the start of their career, and so many examples of players coming back even stronger. 100% he will be one of those who say maybe this injury makes me even stronger and more ready to play at an even higher level."

‌



Potential return date - 2027

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Alisson Becker

The goalkeeper had been aiming to back towards the end of the month has been sidelined since last month's Champions League win over Mamardashvili was forced off during the Merseyside Derby. Although the precise nature of his problem has not been revealed, Giorgi Mamardashvili has stepped in as cover - though he too picked up a problem during the Merseyside derby.

‌



Taking to social media, Alisson hinted that he Galatasaray, writing: "I didn't suffer a new injury. I'm in the treatment phase, and the plan is to be in full playing condition by the end of April!"

But Alisson isn't now expected to return to the fold until the trip to Manchester United on Sunday week. Slot has also said of the goalkeeper: "Towards the end of the season, we expect him to be fit."

View 4 Images Alisson has already missed several crucial Liverpool fixtures with his injury

‌



Potential return date - May 3 vs Manchester United

Giorgi Mamardashvili

Liverpool's goalkeeping troubles went from bad to worse when Carabao Cup at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday with a knee problem. The Georgian was carried off on a stretcher as Freddie Woodman was brought on as his replacement, while the Reds claimed a 2-1 victory over Everton.

Reflecting on the goalkeeper following the final whistle, Slot said: "He is gone off to hospital. It looked to me, and it is also what they told me, an open wound. It will not be a long term injury let's see if he will be available next week."

‌



Early reports have claimed the goalkeeper will be absent for about three weeks, which opens the door for Woodman to continue on Saturday against Palace.

Potential return date - May 9 vs Chelsea

Giovanni Leoni

View 4 Images Giovanni Leoni remains out with an ACL injury (Image: (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images))

‌



Giovanni Leoni has been absent from Liverpool's squad since Japan on his debut against Southampton in the suffering a ruptured ACL back in September. It has since been reported that the centre-back is unlikely to pull on a Liverpool shirt again until next season.

Potential return date - Next season

Wataru Endo

Wataru Endo has been on the sidelines since picking up a foot injury requiring surgery during February's away fixture at the Stadium of Light against Sunderland AFC. While he is anticipated to be fit in time to represent Japan at the World Cup, his Liverpool campaign is effectively over.

‌



Potential return date - This summer

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Conor Bradley

Conor Bradley has also been sidelined since Liverpool's 0-0 draw with Arsenal back in January, after sustaining a knee injury late in the match. The full-back is similarly unlikely to feature again until next campaign.

Sports.title: EFL clubs reject VAR challenge system in Championship
Sports.content:
EFL clubs have opposed the introduction of a VAR challenge system for managers in the Championship.

Sky Sports News understands the idea was proposed by PGMO, which is English football's refereeing governing body.

EFL clubs were given a demonstration of how it would work at last month's annual meeting and provided their feedback.

As a result, there will continue to be no VAR in the EFL next season, just goal-line technology in the Championship.

VAR currently unpopular in the Premier League - but powers extended

VAR is set to continue in the Premier League, despite a recent survey showing its current unpopularity.

At the end of March, the Football Supporters' Association held a survey for 8,000 fans of the 20 Premier League clubs.

75 per cent of the fans said they were against the use of VAR, while 90 per cent disagreed that the introduction of VAR in the Premier League has improved the matchday experience.

91 per cent of fans said VAR has harmed the spontaneity of goal celebrations, while 94 per cent disagreed that VAR makes watching football on television more enjoyable.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Arne Slot bemoans VAR after Liverpool had a penalty overturned against PSG, but have the Reds been hard done by with these types of decisions all season?

All the while, VAR's powers have been extended by football's lawmakers.

Using VAR to check corners will be an option for competitions from this summer, while the core VAR protocol has now been widened to cover second yellow cards.

Lawmakers are adamant that VAR checks on corners must not delay the kick being taken and will only be used to spot obvious errors. Corner-kick checks will be an option, rather than a mandatory part of the VAR protocol.

VARs will also only check incorrectly-awarded second yellow cards. They will not advise referees to issue a second yellow card where one was not shown on the field.

Sports.title: Five Championship players catching the eye of Premier League clubs
Sports.content:
Ahead of the summer transfer window and the conclusion of the Championship season, a number of players are already generating interest from the Premier League.

From a Player of the Season award winner to consistent midfield anchors and a winger in the Team of the Season, Sky Sports News reveals five Championship players who are catching the eye of clubs in the top flight.

Hayden Hackney (Middlesbrough)

Hayden Hackney has been one of the Championship's most consistent midfielders and a player Premier League clubs have been looking at closely.

The 23-year-old was named the Championship's Player of the Season. He has scored five goals in the League and provided eight assists.

Hackney's contract runs until 2027. Middlesbrough are still pushing for promotion, and do not want to see Hackney leave.

A number of clubs have been linked - Premier League-bound Coventry City the latest, while Everton, Tottenham, Leeds United and Manchester United are all understood to have shown interest in the past.

Imran Louza (Watford)

Imran Louza looks like a different player to the one who struggled to make an impact in the Premier League with Watford in 2021/22 - and his output reflects that.

Louza has scored seven goals and has nine assists in 39 Sky Bet Championship matches so far this season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Imran Louza tells Sky Sports about his style of captaincy after being handed the armband permanently at Watford

He has two years remaining on his Watford deal. Promotion to the Premier League is now out of reach for the Hornets - and he is likely to attract attention this summer.

Leo Scienza (Southampton)

Leo Scienza has played a key role in Southampton's recent form and their push for promotion since a September move from 1. FC Heidenheim.

If the Saints return to the Premier League, they will expect the 27-year-old to be part of that squad. If not, his performances are likely to bring interest from elsewhere.

His team-mate, Shea Charles, has also been attracting attention, and is another reason why Southampton could do with going up.

Southampton are in a strong position with Scienza as his contract runs until the summer of 2029.

Ethan Galbraith (Swansea City)

Ethan Galbraith has flourished this season, becoming a creative focal point for Swansea and impressing on the international stage with Northern Ireland.

He caught the eye of Gianfranco Zola during the play-off defeat to Italy.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ethan Galbraith tells Sky Sports about his EFL journey so far and growing up at Man Utd

Galbraith's contract runs until 2028, with the club holding an option to extend by a year.

Galbraith has rejected Swansea's initial offer of a new contract, which is understood to fall short of the terms offered to some of the club's other high performers. Talks are expected to continue.

There has been interest from Premier League and Championship clubs, although no formal offers have materialised since Wrexham had a bid rejected in January.

Head coach Vitor Matos recently said he would like the 24-year-old to remain at the club for the next decade.

Femi Azeez (Millwall)

Millwall's Femi Azeez has been one of the Championship's standout attacking players this season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Femi Azeez tells Sky Sports about his incredible form for Millwall this season, which has helped spark their promotion push

Also named in the Team of the Season, the winger has contributed eight goals and seven assists so far.

Azeez - who was playing for Wealdstone in the National League South as recently as 2018/19 - has two years remaining on his current deal. Millwall are still fighting for automatic promotion.

Sports.title: Slot expected to continue at Liverpool next season
Sports.content:
Arne Slot is expected to continue as Liverpool head coach next season, Sky Sports News understands, as the club close in on Champions League qualification.

Any doubts about the Dutchman's future appear to be subsiding rapidly as a seven-point gap has opened up between Liverpool in fifth place and Chelsea in sixth.

Fifth place will secure Champions League football next season after Arsenal's progression to the semi-finals - and Liverpool's form has picked up while Chelsea are slipping.

Slot, who led Liverpool to the Premier League title last season, has come under pressure during his second campaign, with the Reds set to end the season without a trophy and well off the pace set by Arsenal and Manchester City.

"There's probably a split in the Liverpool supporters over whether he should stay or go, but the noises I am hearing is Slot will be the Liverpool manager next season if they can secure Champions League qualification, which they look like doing right now."

Sky Sports News understands that is the case after a season of increasing speculation over Slot's future, as a transitional season at Anfield has borne frustrations on and off the pitch.

Van Dijk offers honest assessment of 'below-standard' Liverpool season after derby win

"We've got five more games left against teams that are also fighting for the Champions League spots," Van Dijk told Sky Sports after the derby win.

"Every game is a big one. We are very disappointed as a whole for the season that we're having, because of the quality we have. It's below standard.

"But we have to keep fighting, keep going, and make the best out of this poor season we're having. That's the reality, on to the next. Everton was a good three points, and next up is Crystal Palace at home, who we couldn't beat for many, many games before.

"[The situation] is definitely not Liverpool-worthy, in my opinion, but it is the reality, and it was important we got the win. I'm glad we did."

Sports.title: Whittaker says his showboating can lead to 'complete domination’
Sports.content:
Expect Ben Whittaker's viral showboating to remain a key facet of his boxing, even though he is on a run of three double-quick knockout victories.

Whittaker, an Olympic silver medallist, shot to prominence as a professional fighter as he displayed outrageous showboating and showmanship in his contests.

More recently, though, his quick-finishing instincts have come to the fore.

Since his contentious draw with Liam Cameron, when Whittaker tumbled out of the ring and could not continue, the Olympic silver medallist has won three fights in two rounds or less.

He took out Cameron in the second round of their rematch last year and then dispatched Benjamin Gavazi and Braian Suarez, winning both of those contests with stunning first-round knockouts.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Whittaker showed his power in his rematch with Liam Cameron

Whittaker has taken those wins so rapidly that there has been no time for him to display his trademark showboating.

"If the shot's there to take them out, I'll take it," Whittaker told Sky Sports. "I've been working on sitting on the shots, punching through the target, hurting them."

The showboating, though, is a part of his style.

"Andy (Lee, Whittaker's trainer) knows as well it's very unique, it's different. When I can be disciplined I'm a great boxer, too. So it's just marrying the two. Knowing when to do it, when not to do it," Whittaker said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look at Ben Whittaker's showboats in his dominant display over Ezra Arenyeka

He intends to use it as another tool in his approach and he is convinced that his skillset can take him to the top of the sport.

"Of course it's my own style, but I did get a lot of it coming through the amateurs, seeing (Cuba's Julio Cesar) La Cruz, they would win rounds sometimes not throwing punches, they would win from dominating just making someone miss and that's the beauty to me of boxing, being able to win a round off maybe two jabs and making someone miss - that's when you've got complete domination," he said.

"I fell in love with that style. It is a hard style to come up against or to even use yourself.

"A lot of people see it as disrespectful, this and that - it's just a different art. Just like people knock out people, it's another art.

"So for me it's a way of doing something different and seeing different looks. It's a good skill to have."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ben Whittaker once again put on a display to entertain the fans at London's O2 Arena during his points victory over Leon Willings

He added: "Those great fighters, Willie Pep, George Benton, even Pernell Whitaker, these fighters, they had their own style.

"A lot of people have it in their own way and I've just got it in my own way. It's a unique style and when you do it right, it comes off beautiful."

After his victory over Suarez, Whittaker is expected to box in the US in the summer and then return to the UK. A match up with a domestic rival, like Joshua Buatsi or Anthony Yarde, before the end of the year would be ideal.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ben Whittaker and Prince Naseem Hamed have both been known to entertain fans with their repertoire of showboating skills - but who does it best?

"Domestic clashes are what people want to see, so something like that back in England," he said. "As an armchair fan, when I was a kid watching those fights like (George) Groves and (Carl) Froch, they were the ones that got you out of your seat," he said.

"If I could emulate something like that, that would be great but I suppose they're on their own path, I'm on my own path, so we'll see."

But given the threshold for survival could be 38 points, according to Opta, Forest might only be one win away from safety having moved to 36 with Sunday's crucial victory over Burnley.

"If they could win this game against Sunderland, that would put them on 39 and you would be thinking, 'they're not far away now."

Spurs worse off for injuries

Spurs received a boost against Brighton as James Maddison returned to their squad for the first time this season following a knee injury. Although the 29-year-old was an unused substitute, his inclusion raised hopes he could feature before the season is over.

Kulusevski, arguably their most important attacking player alongside Maddison, has not featured all season.

West Ham, by contrast, have an almost clean bill of health. According to Premier Injuries, their only injured player is third-choice goalkeeper Lukasz Fabianski, giving Nuno considerably more options than his Spurs counterpart De Zerbi.

They give Spurs a 58.3 per cent relegation probability following the latest round of Premier League fixtures. It is significantly higher than West Ham's 36.9 per cent probability.
